/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 26-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by the police after threatening to harm his roommate earlier today. He reports that someone on the radio told him to do so. His family reports that, during the past two years, the patient has become increasingly more withdrawn from family and friends. He states that he has spent the majority of the last year alone in his room “working on a project at home to save the earth from an evil alien power.” There is no family history of serious illness. He has smoked marijuana on a daily basis since he was thirteen. Vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, he has a flat affect and his speech is disorganized. An MRI scan of the head is most likely to show which of the following?

Options:
A. Periventricular plaques and white matter lesions
B. Nucleus caudatus atrophy
C. Ring-enhancing lesion
D. Hyperintense temporal lobe lesion
E. Enlarged cerebral ventricles

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question asks about MRI findings associated with a psychiatric disorder (schizophrenia), which falls within the scope of mental disorders and their clinical correlates."}
